text:
Aria (infra): :rotating_light: Seeing a large latency spike in eu-central for runtime-batcher starting ~12:03 UTC. P95 climbing from 220ms -> 1.8s and increase in 502s. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/.../d/rt-batcher
alerts-bot: [ALERT] runtime-batcher-eu-central latency_p95 > 1s (12:03 UTC)
Samir: any signs of KV cache evictions or batcher queue backlog?
Aria (infra): queue length on continuous-batcher is +3x. kvcache miss rate up from 8% -> 42%. logs: 
```
2026-03-18T12:04:12Z batcher: enqueue_ms=1200 queue_len=780
2026-03-18T12:04:13Z kvcache: miss key=slot_... hit=false load_time=14ms
2026-03-18T12:04:15Z runtime: 502 upstream_timeout model=redwood-v1-8b
```
Lena: also seeing sporadic network 5xx egress to eu-central storage (S3 class) starting ~12:02. Could be compounding cache warmups.
Theo: We should immediately: 1) throttle low-priority / background requests 2) divert new sessions away from eu-central to na1 and asia1 3) flip to quantized-fallback model for standard tier 4) restart batcher pods in small rolling window.
PJ: I can flip traffic routing flag now. use internal-api: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood/internal/route-override" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"region":"eu-central","action":"divert","targets":["na1","asia1"],"weight":0.35}'
```
Aria (infra): Running the route override now.
Aria (infra): POST returned 200. Routing override id=rov-20260318-12:05. New flow: divert 35% -> na1, 35% -> asia1, keep 30% in eu-central for high-priority only.
alerts-bot: [INFO] route-override rov-20260318-12:05 applied
Samir: I'll throttle background jobs via quota manager: 
```
redwoodctl quota set --service runtime-batcher --priority background --qps 10
```
Samir: Applied. background QPS went from 120 -> 10.
PJ: Also toggling fallback model for standard-tier customers: 
```
redwoodctl feature-flag set fallback-quantized-v2 true --scope=standard
```
PJ: Flag set. New sessions should pick up quantized-fallback variant.
Theo: Request we spin up 4 extra GPU nodes in dedicated eu pool as a short-term bump.
Aria (infra): Initiating scale: 
```
infractl gpu-pool scale --pool eu-dedicated-primary --add 4 --reason "latency spike 2026-03-18"
```
Aria (infra): Scale job queued id=scale-8891. Cloud provider shows provisioning in progress.
ops-runbook-bot: [RUNBOOK] If kvcache fragmentation suspected, perform rolling restarts of batcher with drain-time 30s.
Lena: I'll kick rolling restart in batches of 10% to avoid large disruption.
Aria (infra): Starting rolling restart of batcher pods (drain=30s, batch=10%).
Aria (infra): First 10% restarted. Observing healthy reconnects, miss rate flattening from 42% -> 28%. p95 trending down.
Samir: After throttle+divert+restart, P95 back to ~400ms. Still above baseline but improving.
Theo: Good. Keep the routing override until eu cluster is stable and new nodes are fully provisioned.
PJ: Cloud provisioning update: 2/4 nodes active, remaining 2 scheduled.
alerts-bot: [RESOLVED?] runtime-batcher-eu-central latency_p95 lowered to 0.45s (12:18 UTC) - still watching
Aria (infra): Can we keep quantized fallback on for standard tier for next 6 hours and then revert if no regressions? Need postmortem.
Samir: Agreed. I flagged a perf regression in the batching changeset from yesterday that likely increased per-request enqueue time. Ticket created: INFRA-5231.
Lena: I'll open a cloud support case for the egress 5xxs to double-check upstream networking flaps.
Theo: Actions: 1) keep routing override until pool stable 2) keep fallback flag on for 6h 3) investigate batching PR INFRA-5231 4) follow up on runbook improvements for kvcache fragmentation.
Aria (infra): Assigning: INFRA-5231 -> Samir, Cloud case -> Lena, Postmortem draft -> Aria. Will circle back in 2h. :thumbsup:
PJ: Noted. I'll rollback the override when you say go.
Aria (infra): Monitoring dashboards now. p95 at 310ms and trending. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
